hints: There is one robot on every square; each robot independently takes k random legal orthogonal moves.
For each starting square, propagate its probability across up/down/left/right neighbors, dividing equally among legal moves.
For each final square, multiply the chance each robot misses it, then sum those empty-square probabilities.
analogy: Each robot spreads probability across nearby squares; a square is empty only if all 64 robots miss it.
example: At k=1, a corner robot chooses among its two legal neighboring squares with probability 1/2 each; it cannot stay on the corner.
algorithm: For each of 64 starting cells, run k probability steps, distributing equally among its legal up/down/left/right neighbors. For each destination cell multiply (1-probability from start i) across all starts; sum all 64 empty probabilities.
correctness: Robots move independently, so the chance a square is empty is the product of each robot's chance not to be there. The expected number of empty squares is the sum of these probabilities.
complexity: O(64*k*8+64^2) time for the fixed board and O(64) probability storage.
